expectations.text: Skim test: the headline states what broke, the root cause, and the recommended fix in at most three sentences, with what broke in the first; the first sentence of each section carries its claim, and none is a teaser or a qualifier chain.
expectations.evidence: Headline section (lines 5-7) has 3 sentences. S1 states what broke: 'Support search returns "not found" when the typed email differs in case from the email stored at signup.' S2 states the root cause: 'The root cause is in `app/db.py`, which treats the raw typed string as the email identity for every flow.' S3 holds the recommended fix: 'I recommend one normalized email key in `app/db.py` with a uniqueness check ...'. The ## and ### sections open with claims: 'All four email-keyed entry points call `db.find_by_email`, so all four inherit the defect.', '`app/search.py` has no loop to patch.', 'I recommend B.', 'Confirmed with survivors.'. The qualifier 'The fixture has no version history, so I cannot name a commit ...' opens the bold Timeline paragraph inside 'Symptom and scope', not a section, so it is not counted against the section-lead rule.
